    <item>
      <title>How I Found OpenStreetMap</title>
      <link>https://www.openstreetmap.org/user/tastywater/diary/409542</link>
      <guid>https://www.openstreetmap.org/user/tastywater/diary/409542</guid>
      <description><p dir="auto">I used to play <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingress_(video_game)" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer">Ingress</a>. For those who haven’t heard of it, you have probably heard of its younger (more popular) sibling, <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pokémon_Go" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer">Pokémon Go</a>, especially if you had to deal with map vandalism from its playerbase. When I acquired my first smartphone, mobile games were still a new thing, and they were mostly full of gimmicks. They never captured the same level of immersion that you could experience when playing a computer or home console game. But when a friend introduced me to Ingress, it was unique, and I was instantly hooked. The storytelling turned me into an “agent” and my phone into an “XM scanner,” just like the cool sci-fi stuff I’d seen in movies. But it was more than just a gimmick, because going somewhere in the real world and coordinating with other players was an integral part of the game. I met a lot of people because of Ingress, and travelled to some amazing places I wouldn’t have otherwise. But as with any game you spend hours and hours playing, I eventually got burned out.</p>

<p dir="auto">A few years ago, I remember hearing about <a href="https://streetcomplete.app" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer">StreetComplete</a>, a gamified way to contribute to OpenStreetMap by solving quests. It sounded like a more productive way to fill the time I had been using for Ingress, while still scratching the itch to explore. As of this writing, the iOS StreetComplete app has only been published for a week, so needless to say, I couldn’t use it on my iPhone back then. When discussion of <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Automatic_number-plate_recognition#United_States" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer">ALPRs</a> came up in the United States more recently, I saw OpenStreetMap mentioned again, and this time I had an Android phone. I downloaded StreetComplete, and have been contributing as a hobby on and off ever since.</p>
</description>

    <item>
      <title>State of the addresses in Belgium - October 2026</title>
      <link>https://www.openstreetmap.org/user/juminet/diary/409540</link>
      <guid>https://www.openstreetmap.org/user/juminet/diary/409540</guid>
      <description><p dir="auto">How complete are addresses in OpenStreetMap in Belgium? After several status these previous years (see <a href="https://www.openstreetmap.org/user/juminet/diary/399972" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer">September 22</a>, <a href="https://www.openstreetmap.org/user/juminet/diary/401542" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer">May 23</a>, <a href="https://www.openstreetmap.org/user/juminet/diary/404116" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer">May 24</a>, <a href="https://www.openstreetmap.org/user/juminet/diary/405543" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer">November 24</a> for Wallonia and <a href="https://www.openstreetmap.org/user/juminet/diary/406654" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer">April 2025 for all Belgium</a>), here is an update of the situation.</p>

<p dir="auto">The aim of this small article is to assess the completeness of addresses in Belgium for OSM, compared to official data. Basically we count the address points in OSM and in official data by municipalities. We don’t check the address quality here, we know there can be errors in OSM data, as well as in official data.</p>

<h3 dir="auto" id="how-i-proceeded">How I proceeded</h3>

<p dir="auto">Using QGIS, I gathered OSM addresses and official ones. OSM data is imported in a PostgreSQL database using ´osm2pgsql´ based on a pbf file for Belgium from the 20th of October. Official data is coming from <a href="https://opendata.bosa.be/index.fr.html" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer">BEST address</a>, that gathers Belgian addresses for the 3 regions of the country.</p>

<p dir="auto">Addresses in OSM can be mapped on buildings (most of the cases), hence on a way, or on a node. I consider only objects with the “addr:housenumber” tag. First, I made a single layer of addresses points from OSM data by merging the centroids of buildings with this tag and the points with this tag, by excluding the places where these two layers overlaps (typically points with an address inside a building where there is already an address). The method is far from perfect: I don’t consider relations, I miss some way objects with addresses but without the building tag (typically some schools), and probably a lot of other edge cases due to the “joyeux bordel” of the OSM data model. Finally I removed duplicate located at the same place.</p>

<p dir="auto">Official data considers several address points for each building unit, or box number. It means that there are often several points at the same place, especially in cities, accounting for each box number. Since the mapping of box number is often not so used in OSM, I removed all duplicated address located at the same location. This reduces the number of official address from 7,033,422 to 4,578,368.</p>

<p dir="auto">Then I simply count the number of OSM and official address by Belgian municipalities and compare the two.</p>

<p dir="auto">The method and the QGIS project file is now saved in <a href="https://github.com/nobohan/osm-vs-best-addresses" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer">github</a>.</p>

<h3 dir="auto" id="the-result-in-maps">The result in maps</h3>

<p dir="auto">In Belgium, I counted 4,098,458 addresses in OSM compared to 4,578,368 in official data: a ratio of 89.5 %. It was 87.6 % in the last analysis in April 2025.</p>

<p dir="auto">But! There are actually a lot of official addresses that are already available but which match no buildings in reality: these are provisioned addresses for future buildings. It is not about a few addresses. In my municipality, about 400 addresses over ~4000 are just provisioned: they do not correspond to buildings already built at the moment. The completeness rate of many places could thus be 10% higher!</p>

<p dir="auto">Here is the map of the completeness by municipalities</p>

<p dir="auto"><img src="http://www.nobohan.be/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/count-be-scaled.jpeg" alt="Map of address completion" loading="lazy"></p>

<p dir="auto">Here is a map with circles showing the number of missing addresses by municipalities. The largest missing parts are in big cities: Antwerpen, Gent, Tournai, Namur, … Brussels region looks however good, and Charleroi improved a lot since the last analysis.</p>

<p dir="auto"><img src="http://www.nobohan.be/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/diff-be-scaled.jpeg" alt="Map of missing addresses" loading="lazy"></p>

<p dir="auto">Municipalities where the completeness rate is the lowest are:</p>

<ol dir="auto">
  <li>Opwijk</li>
  <li>Maarkedal</li>
  <li>Vleteren</li>
  <li>Mont-de-l’Enclus</li>
  <li>Celles</li>
  <li>Berlare</li>
  <li>Ronse</li>
  <li>Estaimpuis</li>
  <li>Huldenberg</li>
  <li>Zwevegem</li>
</ol>

<h3 dir="auto" id="where-are-the-missing-addresses-and-why">Where are the missing addresses and why?</h3>

<p dir="auto">I had a look at some places where OSM is missing addresses compared to official data. It happens in 3 kinds of situations:</p>

<p dir="auto">1) In the municipalities with the lowest completion rate, addresses are missing simply because no contributions were made in these areas: no “manual” adding of addresses nor import of buildings with addresses. Sometimes, the area was actually mapped for a long time in OSM but with buildings without addresses.</p>

<p dir="auto">2) There are a lot of missing addresses in the largest cities: Antwerpen, Gent, Namur, Tournai, … Mapping buildings and addresses is always more complex in cities as compared to mapping small villages. Major reaffectation of land to residential areas (typically from industrial land to residential area) occurs a lot in large cities and we can find a lot of missing addresses in these areas.</p>

<p dir="auto">3) Lastly, even in well-mapped places, there can be missing addresses simply because there are new buildings, either scattered in the streets or gathered in new districts, and the local mapper did not add these new addresses yet.</p>

<p dir="auto">So, we have a completeness rate of about 90% in OpenStreetMap. Given the fact that some official addresses are provisioned, we are not so far from the completion, at least in terms of number of addresses. We know that OSM is sometimes more up-to-date compared to official data, but still there are some places where addresses are just missing.</p>

<h3 dir="auto" id="how-to-improve-the-address-coverage-in-osm-in-belgium">How to improve the address coverage in OSM in Belgium?</h3>

<p dir="auto">The community did already a great job, but there are still some places to improve!</p>

<p dir="auto">If you want to contribute to addresses and buildings in Belgium, you can of course add “by hand” some new buildings and addresses in your neighborhood, or even check existing ones.</p>

<p dir="auto">But actually, a lot of buildings and addresses in Belgium were imported using the “buildings import tool”, which is almost necessary if you want to add thousands of addresses where it is still missing.</p>

<p dir="auto">This tool was just revamped: the new version is available at <a href="https://new.buildings.osm.be/" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" dir="auto">https://new.buildings.osm.be/</a>. Basically, the tool helps to detect where buildings are missing and allows to copy-paste the buildings in JOSM. It takes some times to get used to it, but after a few manipulations, you’ll be ready to import and conflate hundreds of buildings at once.</p>

<p dir="auto">Please ask for some help for any questions about using this tool: there is a <a href="https://matrix.to/#/#osmbe-buildingimport:matrix.org" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer">discussion page here</a>. There are also more information on this <a href="https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/WikiProject_Belgium/Building_and_address_import/AIV_GRB_building_import" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer">wiki page</a>, and you can tell other OSM contributors where you are working using <a href="http://umap.openstreetmap.fr/fr/map/building-import-status_714473#8/49.951/5.400" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer">this map</a>.</p>

</description>

    <item>
      <title>The Church Atlas: a multilingual church map built on OSM data, and what I learned about church tagging</title>
      <link>https://www.openstreetmap.org/user/vetsurgeo/diary/409538</link>
      <guid>https://www.openstreetmap.org/user/vetsurgeo/diary/409538</guid>
      <description><p dir="auto">Hi everyone. I’d like to share a small project built on OpenStreetMap data: The Church Atlas (<a href="https://thechurchatlas.com/?src=osm-diary" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" dir="auto">https://thechurchatlas.com/?src=osm-diary</a>), a free, ad-free map of more than 3,000 churches with an interface in 18 languages.
How it uses OSM: churches are imported city by city from OSM (amenity=place_of_worship with religion=christian), using name and name:xx, denomination, addr:* and wikidata. Wikidata and Wikipedia are then used for summaries, photos and, where OSM has none, street addresses (Wikidata provided addresses for about 600 churches). Every map view and church page credits “© OpenStreetMap contributors” with links to the copyright page and the ODbL.
What I learned about church tagging along the way:
• Many churches, especially small chapels on the Greek islands, only have a name in the local script and no name:en, so they are hard to show in other languages.
• Many chapels share identical names in the same municipality, which makes them hard to tell apart without a locality.
• Some objects carry only addr:housenumber without addr:street, which is not usable as an address on its own.
• Some churches have no denomination tag.
I’m not a professional programmer and built the site with the help of an AI assistant, so I’d especially value advice from experienced mappers: are there tagging conventions I should follow more closely, or common mistakes in how I read the data? If you spot wrong or missing churches, you can tell me on the site or here. Thanks for all the mapping that makes this possible!</p>
</description>

    <item>
      <title>Hallo von Rücksitzhelden: wer wir sind und warum wir hier korrigieren</title>
      <link>https://www.openstreetmap.org/user/R%C3%BCcksitzhelden/diary/409536</link>
      <guid>https://www.openstreetmap.org/user/R%C3%BCcksitzhelden/diary/409536</guid>
      <description><p dir="auto">Hallo zusammen,</p>

<p dir="auto">hinter diesem Konto steht <a href="https://ruecksitzhelden.de" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer">Rücksitzhelden</a>, eine kleine, kostenlose App für Familien auf langen Autofahrten. Sie zeigt Ausflugsziele und familienfreundliche Restaurants direkt an der Route, jeweils mit dem Umweg in Minuten. Gemacht wird sie von Martin Faust aus Berlin.</p>

<p dir="auto">Für die Restaurants nutzen wir OpenStreetMap-Daten (© OpenStreetMap-Mitwirkende, ODbL). Dabei fällt uns immer wieder etwas auf, und oft melden sich Inhaber direkt bei uns, wenn sich ein Name geändert hat oder die Öffnungszeiten nicht mehr stimmen. Diese Korrekturen wollen wir nicht nur bei uns eintragen, sondern auch an OSM zurückgeben.</p>

<p dir="auto">So arbeiten wir:</p>

<ul dir="auto">
  <li><strong>Nur einzelne Korrekturen von Hand</strong>, keine automatisierten oder Massenänderungen. Jede Änderung prüft und gibt ein Mensch frei.</li>
  <li><strong>Ein Changeset pro Objekt</strong>, immer mit Kommentar und Quelle.</li>
  <li><strong>Quellen:</strong> die Website oder das Impressum des Betriebs, Auskünfte der Inhaber, eigene Ortskenntnis. Niemals Google Maps oder andere Quellen mit unpassender Lizenz.</li>
  <li><strong>Im Zweifel eine Notiz statt einer Änderung</strong>, zum Beispiel wenn ein Betrieb geschlossen haben soll, wir es aber nicht sicher wissen.</li>
</ul>

<p dir="auto">Wenn euch an einer unserer Änderungen etwas auffällt, schreibt gern einen Kommentar zum Changeset, eine Nachricht an dieses Konto oder eine Mail an <a href="mailto:hallo@ruecksitzhelden.de" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" dir="auto">hallo@ruecksitzhelden.de</a>. Wir antworten und korrigieren.</p>

<p dir="auto">Danke an alle, die OSM möglich machen. Ohne eure Arbeit gäbe es die App so nicht.</p>

<p dir="auto">Martin</p>

<p dir="auto"><em>English summary:</em> This account belongs to Rücksitzhelden (ruecksitzhelden.de), a small free app for families on long car trips in Europe that uses OSM data for restaurants. We fix what restaurant owners tell us or what their own websites state, one object per changeset, by hand and with a human review, never from Google Maps or other incompatible sources. Questions or concerns: comment on the changeset, message this account, or write to <a href="mailto:hallo@ruecksitzhelden.de" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" dir="auto">hallo@ruecksitzhelden.de</a>.</p>
</description>

    <item>
      <title>StravaTracer: рисуйте тропы по тепловой карте Strava в JOSM одним щелчком</title>
      <link>https://www.openstreetmap.org/user/erickdeoliveiraleal/diary/409526</link>
      <guid>https://www.openstreetmap.org/user/erickdeoliveiraleal/diary/409526</guid>
      <description><p dir="auto"><img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/erickdeoliveiraleal/josm-strava-tracer/main/docs/demo.gif" alt="StravaTracer: один щелчок по тепловой карте создаёт тропу длиной 3 км" loading="lazy"></p>

<p dir="auto"><strong>StravaTracer</strong> — новый плагин для JOSM: щёлкните по тропе на тепловой карте Strava, и он нарисует недостающую линию.</p>

<h3 dir="auto" id="section">Что он делает</h3>

<ul dir="auto">
  <li>идёт по центру следа на тепловой карте, а не по его краю;</li>
  <li>подстраивается под популярность тропы, поэтому и малопосещаемые, и популярные тропы работают с одними и теми же настройками;</li>
  <li>перескакивает через прерывистые участки малопосещаемых троп и догружает тайлы, если тропа продолжается;</li>
  <li>не трогает то, что уже нанесено на карту, и соединяет концы новой линии с существующими;</li>
  <li>создаёт одну линию для выбранной тропы; ответвления можно добавлять по одному.</li>
</ul>

<p dir="auto">Всё это одна команда: Ctrl+Z отменяет её.</p>

<h3 dir="auto" id="section-1">Как пользоваться</h3>

<ol dir="auto">
  <li>Установите <strong>stravatracer</strong> в JOSM: <em>Настройки → Модули</em> (JOSM 19613 или новее).</li>
  <li>Откройте слой тепловой карты Strava. Проще всего это сделать с помощью расширения для браузера <a href="https://github.com/zekefarwell/josm-strava-heatmap" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer">JOSM Strava Heatmap</a>: оно само настраивает URL и cookies.</li>
  <li>Выберите режим <strong>Strava trace</strong> на левой панели инструментов и щёлкните по тропе.</li>
</ol>

<p dir="auto">🎬 <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=B0Jxzoc-fMQ" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer">Видео с демонстрацией</a></p>

<h3 dir="auto" id="section-2">Всегда проверяйте</h3>

<p dir="auto">Тепловая карта показывает, где ходят люди, но не то, существует ли там настоящая дорога и какого она типа. Сверяйте результат со снимками, ставьте правильные теги (по умолчанию <code dir="auto">highway=path</code>) и отправляйте только то, в чём уверены.</p>

<p dir="auto">Код, документация и сообщения об ошибках: <a href="https://github.com/erickdeoliveiraleal/josm-strava-tracer" dir="auto" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer">https://github.com/erickdeoliveiraleal/josm-strava-tracer</a>. Буду рад отзывам!</p>

<p dir="auto">Плагин основан на идее и алгоритме <a href="https://github.com/archie83/osm-strava" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer">osm-strava</a>.</p>
</description>

    <item>
      <title>StravaTracer : tracez les sentiers de la carte de chaleur Strava dans JOSM en un clic</title>
      <link>https://www.openstreetmap.org/user/erickdeoliveiraleal/diary/409525</link>
      <guid>https://www.openstreetmap.org/user/erickdeoliveiraleal/diary/409525</guid>
      <description><p dir="auto"><img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/erickdeoliveiraleal/josm-strava-tracer/main/docs/demo.gif" alt="StravaTracer : un clic sur la carte de chaleur crée un sentier de 3 km" loading="lazy"></p>

<p dir="auto"><strong>StravaTracer</strong> est un nouveau greffon JOSM : cliquez sur un sentier de la carte de chaleur Strava et il dessine la voie manquante.</p>

<h3 dir="auto" id="ce-quil-fait">Ce qu’il fait</h3>

<ul dir="auto">
  <li>il suit le centre de la trace de la carte de chaleur, pas son bord ;</li>
  <li>il s’adapte à la fréquentation du sentier : les sentiers peu et très fréquentés fonctionnent avec les mêmes réglages ;</li>
  <li>il franchit les parties discontinues des sentiers peu fréquentés et télécharge d’autres tuiles quand le sentier continue ;</li>
  <li>il ignore ce qui est déjà cartographié et raccorde les extrémités de la nouvelle voie aux voies existantes ;</li>
  <li>il crée une seule voie pour le sentier cliqué ; les embranchements peuvent être cliqués un par un.</li>
</ul>

<p dir="auto">Tout est une seule commande : Ctrl+Z l’annule.</p>

<h3 dir="auto" id="comment-lutiliser">Comment l’utiliser</h3>

<ol dir="auto">
  <li>Installez <strong>stravatracer</strong> dans JOSM : <em>Préférences → Greffons</em> (JOSM 19613 ou plus récent).</li>
  <li>Ouvrez la couche de la carte de chaleur Strava. Le plus simple est l’extension de navigateur <a href="https://github.com/zekefarwell/josm-strava-heatmap" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer">JOSM Strava Heatmap</a>, qui configure l’URL et les cookies pour vous.</li>
  <li>Choisissez le mode <strong>Strava trace</strong> dans la barre d’outils de gauche et cliquez sur un sentier.</li>
</ol>

<p dir="auto">🎬 <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=B0Jxzoc-fMQ" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer">Vidéo de démonstration</a></p>

<h3 dir="auto" id="vrifiez-toujours">Vérifiez toujours</h3>

<p dir="auto">La carte de chaleur montre où les gens passent, pas s’il existe une vraie voie ni de quel type. Vérifiez le résultat avec l’imagerie, mettez les bons attributs (<code dir="auto">highway=path</code> par défaut) et n’envoyez que ce dont vous êtes sûr.</p>

<p dir="auto">Code, documentation et rapports de bugs : <a href="https://github.com/erickdeoliveiraleal/josm-strava-tracer" dir="auto" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer">https://github.com/erickdeoliveiraleal/josm-strava-tracer</a>. Les retours sont les bienvenus !</p>

<p dir="auto">Le greffon s’appuie sur l’idée et l’algorithme d’<a href="https://github.com/archie83/osm-strava" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer">osm-strava</a>.</p>
</description>

    <item>
      <title>StravaTracer: traza senderos del mapa de calor de Strava en JOSM con un clic</title>
      <link>https://www.openstreetmap.org/user/erickdeoliveiraleal/diary/409524</link>
      <guid>https://www.openstreetmap.org/user/erickdeoliveiraleal/diary/409524</guid>
      <description><p dir="auto"><img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/erickdeoliveiraleal/josm-strava-tracer/main/docs/demo.gif" alt="StravaTracer: un clic en el mapa de calor crea un sendero de 3 km" loading="lazy"></p>

<p dir="auto"><strong>StravaTracer</strong> es un nuevo plugin para JOSM: haz clic sobre un sendero del mapa de calor de Strava y dibuja la vía que falta.</p>

<h3 dir="auto" id="qu-hace">Qué hace</h3>

<ul dir="auto">
  <li>sigue el centro del trazo del mapa de calor, no su borde;</li>
  <li>se adapta a la popularidad del sendero, así que los senderos poco y muy usados funcionan con el mismo ajuste;</li>
  <li>atraviesa los tramos entrecortados de los senderos poco usados y descarga más teselas cuando el sendero continúa;</li>
  <li>ignora lo que ya está mapeado y conecta los extremos de la vía nueva con las vías existentes;</li>
  <li>crea una sola vía para el sendero en el que hiciste clic; los ramales se pueden trazar uno a uno.</li>
</ul>

<p dir="auto">Todo es un único comando: Ctrl+Z lo deshace.</p>

<h3 dir="auto" id="cmo-usarlo">Cómo usarlo</h3>

<ol dir="auto">
  <li>Instala <strong>stravatracer</strong> en JOSM: <em>Preferencias → Complementos</em> (JOSM 19613 o posterior).</li>
  <li>Abre la capa del mapa de calor de Strava. La forma más fácil es la extensión de navegador <a href="https://github.com/zekefarwell/josm-strava-heatmap" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer">JOSM Strava Heatmap</a>, que configura la URL y las cookies por ti.</li>
  <li>Activa el modo <strong>Strava trace</strong> en la barra de herramientas de la izquierda y haz clic sobre un sendero.</li>
</ol>

<p dir="auto">🎬 <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=B0Jxzoc-fMQ" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer">Vídeo de demostración</a></p>

<h3 dir="auto" id="revisa-siempre">Revisa siempre</h3>

<p dir="auto">El mapa de calor muestra por dónde pasa la gente, no si existe una vía real ni de qué tipo es. Comprueba el resultado con las imágenes, pon las etiquetas correctas (<code dir="auto">highway=path</code> por defecto) y sube solo lo que tengas claro.</p>

<p dir="auto">Código, documentación y reportes de errores: <a href="https://github.com/erickdeoliveiraleal/josm-strava-tracer" dir="auto" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer">https://github.com/erickdeoliveiraleal/josm-strava-tracer</a>. ¡Las sugerencias son bienvenidas!</p>

<p dir="auto">El plugin se basa en la idea y el algoritmo de <a href="https://github.com/archie83/osm-strava" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer">osm-strava</a>.</p>
</description>

    <item>
      <title>StravaTracer: trace trilhas do heatmap do Strava no JOSM com um clique</title>
      <link>https://www.openstreetmap.org/user/erickdeoliveiraleal/diary/409523</link>
      <guid>https://www.openstreetmap.org/user/erickdeoliveiraleal/diary/409523</guid>
      <description><p dir="auto"><img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/erickdeoliveiraleal/josm-strava-tracer/main/docs/demo.gif" alt="StravaTracer: um clique no heatmap cria uma trilha de 3 km" loading="lazy"></p>

<p dir="auto">O <strong>StravaTracer</strong> é um novo plugin do JOSM: clique numa trilha do heatmap do Strava e ele desenha a via que falta.</p>

<h3 dir="auto" id="o-que-ele-faz">O que ele faz</h3>

<ul dir="auto">
  <li>segue o centro do traço do heatmap, não a borda;</li>
  <li>se adapta à popularidade da trilha, então trilhas pouco usadas e muito usadas funcionam com o mesmo ajuste;</li>
  <li>atravessa os trechos picotados das trilhas pouco usadas e baixa mais tiles quando a trilha continua;</li>
  <li>ignora o que já está mapeado e liga as pontas da via nova às vias existentes;</li>
  <li>cria uma via só para a trilha clicada; os ramos podem ser clicados um a um.</li>
</ul>

<p dir="auto">Tudo é um único comando: Ctrl+Z desfaz.</p>

<h3 dir="auto" id="como-usar">Como usar</h3>

<ol dir="auto">
  <li>Instale o <strong>stravatracer</strong> no JOSM: <em>Preferências → Plugins</em> (JOSM 19613 ou mais novo).</li>
  <li>Abra a camada do heatmap do Strava. O jeito mais fácil é a extensão de navegador <a href="https://github.com/zekefarwell/josm-strava-heatmap" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer">JOSM Strava Heatmap</a>, que configura a URL e os cookies para você.</li>
  <li>Ative o modo <strong>Strava trace</strong> na barra de ferramentas da esquerda e clique numa trilha.</li>
</ol>

<p dir="auto">🎬 <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=B0Jxzoc-fMQ" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer">Vídeo de demonstração</a></p>

<h3 dir="auto" id="revise-sempre">Revise sempre</h3>

<p dir="auto">O heatmap mostra por onde as pessoas passam, não se ali existe uma via de verdade, nem o tipo dela. Confira o resultado com as imagens, coloque as tags certas (<code dir="auto">highway=path</code> por padrão) e só envie o que você tiver certeza.</p>

<p dir="auto">Código, documentação e relatos de erros: <a href="https://github.com/erickdeoliveiraleal/josm-strava-tracer" dir="auto" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer">https://github.com/erickdeoliveiraleal/josm-strava-tracer</a>. Sugestões são bem-vindas!</p>

<p dir="auto">O plugin é baseado na ideia e no algoritmo do <a href="https://github.com/archie83/osm-strava" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer">osm-strava</a>.</p>
</description>

    <item>
      <title>StravaTracer: trace missing paths from the Strava heatmap in JOSM with one click</title>
      <link>https://www.openstreetmap.org/user/erickdeoliveiraleal/diary/409522</link>
      <guid>https://www.openstreetmap.org/user/erickdeoliveiraleal/diary/409522</guid>
      <description><p dir="auto"><img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/erickdeoliveiraleal/josm-strava-tracer/main/docs/demo.gif" alt="StravaTracer: one click on the heatmap creates a 3 km path" loading="lazy"></p>

<p dir="auto"><strong>StravaTracer</strong> is a new JOSM plugin: click on a trail of the Strava heatmap and it draws the missing way for you.</p>

<h3 dir="auto" id="what-it-does">What it does</h3>

<ul dir="auto">
  <li>follows the centre line of the heatmap trace, not its edge;</li>
  <li>adapts to the popularity of the trail, so rarely and heavily used trails work with the same settings;</li>
  <li>crosses the broken parts of rarely used trails and downloads more tiles when the trail goes on;</li>
  <li>ignores what is already mapped and connects the ends of the new way to the existing ways;</li>
  <li>creates a single way for the clicked trail; branches can be clicked one by one.</li>
</ul>

<p dir="auto">Everything is one command: Ctrl+Z undoes it.</p>

<h3 dir="auto" id="how-to-use-it">How to use it</h3>

<ol dir="auto">
  <li>Install <strong>stravatracer</strong> in JOSM: <em>Preferences → Plugins</em> (JOSM 19613 or newer).</li>
  <li>Open the Strava heatmap layer. The easiest way is the <a href="https://github.com/zekefarwell/josm-strava-heatmap" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer">JOSM Strava Heatmap</a> browser extension, which sets the URL and the cookies for you.</li>
  <li>Select the <strong>Strava trace</strong> mode in the left toolbar and click on a trail.</li>
</ol>

<p dir="auto">🎬 <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=B0Jxzoc-fMQ" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer">Demo video</a></p>

<h3 dir="auto" id="please-review">Please review</h3>

<p dir="auto">The heatmap shows where people go, not whether there is a real way there, nor its type. Check the result with the imagery, set the right tags (<code dir="auto">highway=path</code> by default) and only upload what you are confident about.</p>

<p dir="auto">Code, documentation and bug reports: <a href="https://github.com/erickdeoliveiraleal/josm-strava-tracer" dir="auto" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer">https://github.com/erickdeoliveiraleal/josm-strava-tracer</a>. Feedback is welcome!</p>

<p dir="auto">The plugin is based on the idea and the algorithm of <a href="https://github.com/archie83/osm-strava" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer">osm-strava</a>.</p>
</description>
      <dc:creator>erickdeoliveiraleal</dc:creator>

    <item>
      <title>How to map 1200 tasks on HOT Tasking Manager in 30 minutes.</title>
      <link>https://www.openstreetmap.org/user/anthaas/diary/409518</link>
      <guid>https://www.openstreetmap.org/user/anthaas/diary/409518</guid>
      <description><h3 dir="auto" id="disclaimer-do-not-try-this-at-home"><em>Disclaimer: Do not try this at home!</em></h3>

<p dir="auto">There is an ongoing <a href="https://tasks.hotosm.org/explore?campaign=DRC%20Ebola%202026&amp;difficulty=CHALLENGING&amp;omitMapResults=1&amp;status=PUBLISHED%2CARCHIVED%2CDRAFT&amp;types=LAND_USE" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer">DRC Ebola campaign</a> where mappers are asked to update residential areas. All newly published projects follow the same pattern. There are a lot of small tasks to be mapped. The tasks are so small that no new residential areas need to be mapped in them. Only the existing mapping needs to be updated (move or delete buildings based on the imagery required by the project). Often the task area is completely empty.</p>

<p dir="auto">Since the deployment of the <a href="https://github.com/hotosm/tasking-manager/releases/tag/v5.4.1" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer">v5.4.1 release</a> and the <a href="https://github.com/hotosm/tasking-manager/pull/7130" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer">panel rearrangement</a>, completing a task takes more clicks than in the previous version. Even if you’re an experienced mapper who read the instructions before you started, the Instructions tab still opens first, so you have to switch to the Completion tab and scroll past the additional instructions to submit the task.
Considering the small tasks in the campaign, the time it takes to submit a single task is more than half of the total time spent on mapping.</p>

<h2 dir="auto" id="this-is-where-laziness-kicks-in-and-so-does-the-tasking-manager-api">This is where laziness kicks in. And so does the Tasking Manager API.</h2>
<p dir="auto">The goal? Find patterns and use whatever means to speed up the process.</p>

<h3 dir="auto" id="prerequisites-that-must-be-met">Prerequisites that must be met:</h3>

<ol dir="auto">
  <li>No other mappers are active on the project. This matters because you work within the area defined by the project’s task grid without locking the tasks.</li>
  <li>You upload regularly to prevent conflicts (a mapper who locks a task in the Tasking Manager always takes priority over any changes you made there without locking it).</li>
</ol>

<p dir="auto">Validators may be suspicious when so many tasks are marked as mapped within seconds of each other. This diary documents the process and explains why these tasks met all the requirements to be marked as mapped.</p>

<h3 dir="auto" id="the-technical-workflow-in-josm">The technical workflow in JOSM:</h3>

<ol dir="auto">
  <li>Download the project’s task grid (using the TM API). Each task boundary has its ID and status.</li>
  <li>Using the search function, find the right number of small unmapped tasks with the query <code dir="auto">taskStatus=READY waylength:-300</code> (only the unmapped tasks with a perimeter under 300 meters).</li>
  <li>In the Tags/Memberships window, right-click the <code dir="auto">&lt;X different&gt;</code> value of the <code dir="auto">taskId</code> key and copy the list of values into a text editor for later.</li>
  <li>Use Download along to download all OSM data for the selected tasks as a new layer.</li>
  <li>Now add the task boundaries to the TODO list.</li>
  <li>Inspect the tasks one by one and mark each one as done in the TODO list.</li>
  <li>Upload the data to the OSM server (don’t forget to fill in the project’s changeset comment).</li>
</ol>

<h3 dir="auto" id="the-python-script-outside-josm">The Python script (outside JOSM):</h3>

<ol dir="auto">
  <li>Use the project ID and the saved taskId list as input.</li>
  <li>A small script iterates over the taskId list and calls the TM API to lock each task and mark it as mapped (two API calls per task).</li>
  <li>If the script fails to lock a task, it skips it and moves on to the next one.</li>
</ol>

<p dir="auto">That completes the first iteration, and you can start over. The project’s task grid needs to be downloaded again to get the updated task statuses. Change the search query from <code dir="auto">waylength:-300</code> to <code dir="auto">waylength:-620</code>. The rest of the steps remain the same. Don’t forget to update the taskId list for the script. The third iteration uses <code dir="auto">waylength:-950</code>.</p>

<h2 dir="auto" id="the-result">The result</h2>
<p dir="auto">After three iterations, 70% of the project was mapped and I saved roughly 5,000 mouse clicks and a great deal of time. At the time of writing, I had already used this workflow on five projects and mapped over 4,500 tasks. I didn’t encounter any merge conflicts.</p>

<h2 dir="auto" id="notes">Notes</h2>
<p dir="auto">I found that, for me, the sweet spot is around 200–400 tasks per batch. You can tweak the <code dir="auto">waylength</code> value in the search query (all tasks smaller than…) to achieve the right number of tasks in the selection.
The biggest slowdown was the OpenAerialMap imagery used in the Ebola campaign because its tiles load quite slowly.</p>

<p dir="auto">When I only deleted features in a task, I just moved to the next task and uploaded the data every 100 tasks. If another mapper who locked the task had already deleted the same object, JOSM showed a warning that it no longer existed on the server, and the upload continued. If I added any features to a task, I uploaded the data immediately so my changes were already on the server in case someone else locked the task.</p>

<h2 dir="auto" id="conclusion">Conclusion</h2>
<p dir="auto">On every project, I stopped once all tasks matching <code dir="auto">waylength:-950</code> were done. Larger tasks take longer to update, so bypassing the Tasking Manager brings little benefit, and I suggest returning to the regular workflow with task locking.</p>
</description>

    <item>
      <title>Praha na papíře, OSM v základu</title>
      <link>https://www.openstreetmap.org/user/Jiri%20Podhorecky/diary/409516</link>
      <guid>https://www.openstreetmap.org/user/Jiri%20Podhorecky/diary/409516</guid>
      <description><p dir="auto">Právě vznikla tištěná turistická mapa Prahy, na základě aktuálních dat OpenStreetMap. Je určená lidem, kteří do Prahy přijeli na pár dnů a chtějí se rychle zorientovat v tom nejzajímavějším, co Praha nabízí.</p>

<p dir="auto"><img src="https://opu.peklo.biz/p/26/10/22/1792650316-2ae8e.jpeg" alt="Mapa Prahy 1: 10 000" loading="lazy"></p>

<p dir="auto">Mapový podklad je záměrně jednoduchý. Obsahuje síť ulic a jen nezbytné množství dalších informací. Díky tomu zůstává přehledný a dává prostor tomu dalšímu. Přibližně stovce zajímavých míst, která jsou na mapě vyznačena pomocí malých ilustrací a popisků. Vedle známých historických památek jsou tu i ty méně známé, moderní stavby, veřejné umění nebo technické zajímavosti.</p>

<p dir="auto">Asi vás napadne, proč ještě dnes tisknout mapu, když máme telefony i encyklopedie v kapse. Odpověď je jednoduchá. Nejde o náhradu digitálních map. Ty používáme všichni. Papírová mapa jen nabízí jiný pohled na totéž.</p>

<p dir="auto">Rozložená ukazuje celé historické město najednou. Vidím vzdálenosti mezi místy, představím si  kudy se vydám  na první pohled  - a nechám oči chvíli bloudit po ulicích. Je to trochu pomalejší způsob, jak se zorientovat. A právě v tom je kouzlo map, na které už tak trochu zapomínáme. Na ostrém slunci zůstává čitelná, nepotřebuje baterii a můžete si do ní poznačit tužkou místo, které vás zaujalo. Po návratu domů se mapa promění ve vzpomínku na navštívená místa. Na zadní straně jsou stručné informace o nejvýznamnějších pražských památkách v devíti světových jazycích.  Je to základní přehled bez nutnosti je hledat.</p>

<p dir="auto"><img src="https://opu.peklo.biz/p/26/10/20/1792512095-c8b43.jpeg" alt="Rozložená mapa" loading="lazy"></p>

<p dir="auto">Trochu se chlubím. Graficky jsem ji připravil, vyzkoušel si,  jak na každém milimetru, na každém odstínu záleží. <a href="https://www.velkoobchodmcu.cz/p/praha-plan-mesta-1-10t-mcu" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer">Vydali jsme ji ve vydavatelství, v kterém se turistickým publikacím už nějakou dobu věnujeme.</a>  Je tu vidět síla čerstvých mapových dat, za nimiž stojí komunita a tak trochu i moje znalost rodného města. Míst je hodně, ale vybrat z nich sbírku vzpomínek které mám v srdci, na to už databázový dotaz nestačí. Chtěl jsem ukázat Prahu jako rozmanité a přitom ne zas tak veliké město.  Nejen jako ukazovač tras od startu do cíle.</p>

<p dir="auto">Pokud vám během návštěvy Prahy mapka pomůže jen jednou, splnila účel.   A možná se tak  připomene, že pomalý analogový svět ještě neřekl poslední slovo. S pomocí nových zkušeností je později můžeme propojit s budoucností.</p>
</description>

    <item>
      <title>Prague on Paper, OSM at Its Heart</title>
      <link>https://www.openstreetmap.org/user/Jiri%20Podhorecky/diary/409515</link>
      <guid>https://www.openstreetmap.org/user/Jiri%20Podhorecky/diary/409515</guid>
      <description><p dir="auto">A new printed tourist map of Prague has just been published, built directly on up-to-date OpenStreetMap data. It is designed for visitors who arrive in the capital of the Czech Republic for a few days and want a quick, clear orientation to the very best the city has to offer.</p>

<p dir="auto"><img src="https://opu.peklo.biz/p/26/10/22/1792650316-2ae8e.jpeg" alt="PRAGUE MAP 1:10 000" loading="lazy"></p>

<p dir="auto">In static cartography, the base map is intentionally kept minimal. It features the street network alongside only the essential geographic elements. This clean background leaves ample room for what matters most: roughly one hundred curated points of interest, brought to life with small custom illustrations and brief labels. Beside iconic historical landmarks, the map highlights lesser-known sights, modern architecture, public art, and unique engineering points of interest.</p>

<p dir="auto">You might wonder why anyone would print a physical map today, when we all carry navigation apps and encyclopedias in our pockets. The answer is simple: it isn’t meant to replace digital tools. We all use those daily. A paper map simply offers a different perspective on the same space.</p>

<p dir="auto">Unfolded, it presents the entire historic city at a single glance. You can feel the true distances between places, plot out a walk visually, or simply let your eyes wander across the streets. It invites a slightly slower pace of orientation—a classic form of spatial magic we sometimes forget in the digital age. It stays perfectly legible in bright sunlight, requires no battery, and lets you mark your favorite spots with a pencil. Long after you return home, it turns into a tangible keepsake of your journey. On the back, concise overviews of Prague’s major sights are provided in nine languages, offering quick context without needing to search online.</p>

<p dir="auto"><img src="https://opu.peklo.biz/p/26/10/20/1792512095-c8b43.jpeg" alt="UNFOLDED MAP" loading="lazy"></p>

<p dir="auto">To be a bit personal: I had the privilege of working on the graphic design and cartographic preparation for this project, testing firsthand how much every single millimeter and color nuance matters in print. <a href="https://www.velkoobchodmcu.cz/p/praha-plan-mesta-1-10t-mcu" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer">It was published by our team, where we’ve been crafting travel publications for years.</a> The finished map really showcases the strength of fresh, community-driven OSM data combined with a lifetime of personal knowledge of my hometown.</p>

<p dir="auto">While database queries can easily return thousands of locations, filtering them down to a meaningful collection of memories requires a human touch. I wanted to show Prague as a rich, diverse, yet walkable city—not just calculate the fastest route from point A to point B.</p>

<p dir="auto">If this map helps you navigate or discover something new during your visit, even just once, it has fulfilled its purpose. And perhaps it serves as a gentle reminder that the slow, tactile world still has plenty to offer—especially when powered by open data and brought forward into the future.</p>
</description>
